Online consultations both video and face to face do have limitations and should only be used for conditions that are appropriate for a remote consult. We do have plenty of face-to-face availability both with our GP team and our wider multidisciplinary clinical team including our neighbourhood partners such as the community pharmacy team and the primary care network Additional Roles Reimbursement Scheme (ARRS) healthcare professionals. 

Our tools and protocols assist us and the patient to ensure that the most appropriate modality with the most appropriate healthcare professional is given to the patient based on the medical need presented. 

With regards to your specific issue, it is a little hard understanding what the exact issue was. It seems like you had an online consultation with a pharmacist and either the pharmacist suggested you consult with a GP, or you may have wanted a further consult with a GP. Either way, if appropriate, you can have a consultation with a GP both remotely or onsite. If your original appointment request required a GP, you could have booked a GP, but possibly your original medical query was more appropriate for a pharmacist. As I said, I am not clear what the exact issue you had was. Please feel free to contact the surgery with more details and we can investigate further. 

Best Wishes
Mani

I am sorry that there was a delay in you being seen by our clinician which deviated from the allocated time slot. The whole team works very hard to ensure that appointment timings are kept to. However, the nature of healthcare provision does occasionally lead to delays. 

Your Google name may differ from your actual name, as I cannot find an Annie Li on our system. I would be more than happy to investigate exactly why your appointment was delayed by an hour. Please message me, Mani, directly on apct.admin@nhs.net with your details and I can find out what happened. 

My tentative investigations, based on when we received this review, which was on Monday 23/2/26 in the evening, was that out of the 27 clinical sessions carried out by clinicians on 23/2/26, one session did over run. Looking the appointment data, it looks as though the clinician had a patient that took over 45 minutes to resolve the issue using the one allocated 10 minute slot. This subsequently delayed the remaining session. The team, the clinician and I are sorry for this inconvenience, but the medical issue was an emergency which had to be addressed. I would have hoped that our reception team would have kept the patients informed of delay. 

We do strive to ensure the patients are seen on time, but on this occasion clearly this did not happen. We will try and do better. Thank you.

BW
